prompt: Some people believe that all students should wear a school uniform, while others think students should be free to choose their own clothes. To what extent do you agree or disagree that school uniforms should be compulsory?
ideas: Uniforms make everyone equal, so poorer students are not judged
They save parents time and money on clothes
But they can limit how young people express their personality

prompt: Some people think it is better to study in a traditional classroom with a teacher, while others believe that online courses are a more effective way to learn. Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.
ideas: Classrooms give face-to-face support and help students stay motivated
Online courses are flexible and cheaper, especially for working adults
Your view: a mix of both may suit most learners

prompt: In many countries, more and more people are moving from the countryside to live in big cities. Do the advantages of this trend outweigh the disadvantages?
ideas: Cities offer more jobs, better hospitals and universities
Cities are crowded, expensive and polluted
Villages lose young people and local traditions

prompt: In many parts of the world, the number of overweight children is increasing. What are the main causes of this problem, and what measures could be taken to solve it?
ideas: Causes: fast food, sugary drinks and too much screen time
Children walk less and play outside less than before
Solutions: healthy school meals, more PE lessons, education for parents

prompt: In many families today, people rarely sit down and eat a meal together. Why is this happening? Is this a positive or negative development?
ideas: Parents work long hours and children have busy schedules
People eat in front of screens or order food separately
Shared meals help families talk, so losing them is mostly negative

prompt: Some people say that children under the age of twelve should not be allowed to have their own smartphone. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
ideas: Phones help parents contact children and keep them safe
Young children can see harmful content or become addicted
A simple phone without internet could be a compromise

prompt: Some people believe that working from home is better for employees, while others think that working in an office is more productive. Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.
ideas: Home: no commuting, more time with family, quieter for some people
Office: easier teamwork, clear routine, fewer distractions for others
Your view: it depends on the job and the person

prompt: Nowadays, many people buy almost everything online instead of going to shops. What are the advantages and disadvantages of this?
ideas: It is convenient, often cheaper and saves time
You cannot try products, and deliveries create waste and traffic
Local shops close and town centres become empty

prompt: Traffic congestion is becoming a serious problem in many cities around the world. What are the causes of this problem, and what solutions can you suggest?
ideas: Causes: more private cars and poor public transport
Cities were not designed for so many vehicles
Solutions: better buses and trains, cycle lanes, charges for driving in the centre

prompt: These days, fewer young people read books for pleasure than in the past. Why do you think this is? What can be done to encourage young people to read more?
ideas: Phones, games and videos compete for their free time
Schools often make reading feel like homework
Solutions: free libraries, book clubs, letting children choose what to read

prompt: Some people think that physical education should be a compulsory subject for all students until they finish school. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
ideas: Exercise improves health and concentration in class
Team sports teach cooperation and discipline
Some students hate sport, so schools should offer a choice of activities

prompt: Some people prefer to spend their holidays travelling abroad, while others think it is better to explore their own country. Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.
ideas: Abroad: new cultures, languages and experiences
At home: cheaper, easier, supports the local economy
Many people have never seen the best places in their own country

prompt: Many students have a part-time job while they are studying at university. Do the advantages of this outweigh the disadvantages?
ideas: Students earn money and become more independent
They gain work experience and useful skills for their CV
But jobs can take time away from studying and cause stress

prompt: In many towns and cities, the streets and parks are often full of litter. What are the causes of this problem, and what measures could be taken to solve it?
ideas: Causes: not enough bins, too much packaging, people do not care
Fines are rarely given to people who drop litter
Solutions: more bins, higher fines, teaching children in school

prompt: In some countries, young adults are living with their parents for much longer than they did in the past. What are the reasons for this? Is this a positive or negative trend?
ideas: Housing is very expensive and salaries for young people are low
Students study for longer before starting work
Positive: families stay close; negative: young people become less independent

prompt: Some people believe that public transport, such as buses and trains, should be free for everyone. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
ideas: More people would leave their cars at home, reducing pollution
It would help people on low incomes
But someone must pay, probably through higher taxes

prompt: Some people think that parents have the most important influence on a child's development, while others believe that teachers and schools play a bigger role. Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.
ideas: Parents shape values, habits and behaviour from birth
Teachers give knowledge and social skills over many years
Your view: both matter, but parents set the foundation

prompt: An increasing number of students choose to go abroad to study at university. What are the advantages and disadvantages of this?
ideas: Students learn a language and become more independent
They may get better job opportunities later
But it is expensive, and students can feel lonely or homesick

prompt: Many people today say that they feel stressed in their everyday lives. What are the main causes of stress, and what can be done to reduce it?
ideas: Causes: long working hours, money worries, always being online
People do not have enough time to rest or exercise
Solutions: flexible work, sport and hobbies, limits on work emails

prompt: Nowadays, many people rarely cook meals at home and prefer to buy ready-made food or eat in restaurants. Why is this happening? Is this a positive or negative development?
ideas: People are busy, and food delivery apps are very easy to use
Many young people never learned to cook
Negative for health and money, but positive for restaurants and jobs

prompt: Some people believe that in the future, computers and artificial intelligence will replace teachers in the classroom. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
ideas: AI can give each student personal practice and instant feedback
Teachers motivate, support and understand students' feelings
AI will probably be a tool for teachers, not a replacement

prompt: Some people think that governments should spend money on the arts, such as music, theatre and museums. Others believe this money should be spent on public services like healthcare and education. Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.
ideas: Arts protect culture, attract tourists and improve quality of life
Health and education are basic needs that affect everyone
Arts usually need only a small part of the budget

prompt: International tourism has become one of the largest industries in the world. Do the advantages of international tourism outweigh the disadvantages for the countries that tourists visit?
ideas: Tourism creates jobs and brings foreign money
It can damage nature and raise prices for local people
Traditional culture may become a show for tourists

prompt: Plastic waste is causing serious damage to the oceans and wildlife. What are the main causes of this problem, and what solutions can you suggest?
ideas: Causes: single-use packaging and poor recycling systems
Plastic from rivers and beaches ends up in the sea
Solutions: ban single-use plastics, deposit schemes for bottles, cleaner packaging

prompt: Children today see more advertisements than ever before, especially online. What effects does this have on children? What can be done to protect them?
ideas: Children want more products and may pressure their parents
Adverts for junk food can harm their health
Solutions: stricter rules on online ads and teaching media literacy

prompt: Some people think that the best way to reduce crime is to give longer prison sentences. Others believe that education and job training for prisoners are more effective. To what extent do you agree that longer prison sentences are the best solution?
ideas: Long sentences may frighten some people away from crime
But many prisoners commit crimes again after release
Training and jobs give former prisoners a real alternative

prompt: Some people believe that the retirement age should be raised because people are living longer. Others think that older people should be able to stop working earlier. Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.
ideas: Working longer helps pay for pensions and keeps people active
Physical jobs are very hard for older workers
Older workers may block jobs for young people

prompt: Large international companies are now opening branches in almost every country. Do the advantages of this outweigh the disadvantages?
ideas: They create jobs and bring new technology and investment
Small local businesses may not be able to compete
Every city starts to look the same, losing its local character

prompt: In many countries, the proportion of older people in the population is increasing. What problems does this cause, and what solutions can you suggest?
ideas: Problems: higher healthcare and pension costs, fewer workers
Many older people feel lonely or isolated
Solutions: flexible work for older people, better care services, community programmes

prompt: Many young people today see celebrities, such as singers and influencers, as their role models. Why is this the case? Is this a positive or negative situation?
ideas: Celebrities are everywhere on social media and seem exciting
Some promote good causes and healthy lifestyles
Others show unrealistic lives that make young people feel bad

prompt: Some people think that spending large amounts of money on space exploration is a waste, and that this money should be used to solve problems on Earth. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
ideas: Problems like poverty and disease need money now
Space research has led to useful technologies, such as satellites
It may help humanity in the long term

prompt: Some people believe that university education should be free for all students, while others think that students should pay for their own studies. Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.
ideas: Free education gives equal chances to poorer students
Society benefits from more educated people
Paying fees may make students value their studies more and saves public money

prompt: In the near future, driverless cars may become common on our roads. Do the advantages of this development outweigh the disadvantages?
ideas: Fewer accidents caused by human error
Older and disabled people could travel independently
Drivers may lose jobs, and the technology could fail or be hacked

prompt: In many major cities, house prices and rents have become too expensive for ordinary people. What are the causes of this problem, and what measures could be taken to solve it?
ideas: Causes: more people moving to cities and not enough new homes
Properties are bought as investments or used for holiday rentals
Solutions: build affordable housing, control rents, develop smaller towns

prompt: Nowadays, many people get their news from social media rather than from newspapers or television. Why is this happening? Is this a positive or negative development?
ideas: Social media is free, fast and always on our phones
News can be shared and discussed instantly
But false information spreads easily and people see only one side

prompt: Professional sports players earn far more money than people in important jobs such as nurses and teachers. Some people think this is unfair. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
ideas: Nurses and teachers contribute more to society
Athletes' careers are short and very few reach the top
Their salaries come from fans and sponsors, not the government

prompt: Some people believe that success in life is mainly measured by how much money a person earns. Others think that personal happiness and relationships are more important. Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.
ideas: Money brings security, comfort and opportunities
Many rich people are still unhappy or lonely
Your view: enough money matters, but happiness defines success

prompt: English is now used as an international language in business, science and travel. What are the advantages and disadvantages of having one global language?
ideas: Easier communication between countries and cultures
More access to information and international jobs
Local languages and cultures may slowly disappear

prompt: In many countries, it is difficult for young people to find a job after they finish their education. What are the reasons for this, and what can be done to improve the situation?
ideas: Employers want experience that graduates do not have
Education does not always teach practical skills
Solutions: internships, apprenticeships, better career advice at school

prompt: In many societies, people buy far more things than they actually need. Why do people do this? What are the effects on individuals and the environment?
ideas: Advertising and social media create new desires
Cheap products and easy credit make buying simple
Effects: debt and stress for people, waste and pollution for the planet

prompt: Some people think that old buildings in city centres should be protected, even if this makes it harder to build modern housing and offices. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
ideas: Old buildings show a city's history and identity
They attract tourists and make cities attractive
But cities also need space to grow and modernise

prompt: Some people believe that scientific research should be carefully controlled by governments. Others think that scientists should be free to choose what they research. Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.
ideas: Control prevents dangerous or unethical experiments
Freedom leads to unexpected discoveries
Governments may support only research that brings quick profit

prompt: In some countries, it is common for young people to take a year off between finishing school and starting university, to travel or work. Do the advantages of this outweigh the disadvantages?
ideas: Students become more mature and know what they want to study
They gain life experience and work skills
Some never return to studying, and travel can be expensive

prompt: In many countries, traditional customs and skills are disappearing as society becomes more modern. What are the causes of this problem, and what can be done to protect these traditions?
ideas: Young people move to cities and follow global culture
Traditional crafts do not pay well
Solutions: teach traditions in schools, support local festivals, fund craftspeople

prompt: Thanks to better healthcare, people today are living much longer than in the past. What effects does this have on society? How can individuals prepare for a longer life?
ideas: More pressure on health systems and pensions
Grandparents can spend more time with families and share experience
Individuals should save money early and stay physically active

prompt: Some people believe that governments should put a high tax on unhealthy food and sugary drinks to improve public health. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
ideas: Higher prices may change what people buy
The money could pay for health services
It may be unfair to poorer families and limits personal choice

prompt: Some people think that private cars should be banned from city centres. Others believe this would cause serious problems for residents and businesses. Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.
ideas: Cleaner air, less noise and safer streets for pedestrians
Shops may lose customers, and some people need cars
Good public transport must come first

prompt: Many countries compete to host major international sports events such as the Olympic Games or the World Cup. What are the advantages and disadvantages of hosting such events?
ideas: Tourism, international attention and new infrastructure
Very high costs and stadiums that are not used afterwards
Local people may be moved from their homes to make space

prompt: Crimes committed through the internet, such as online fraud and identity theft, are increasing rapidly. Why is this happening, and what can be done to reduce this type of crime?
ideas: More of our lives and money are online
Criminals can work from other countries and are hard to catch
Solutions: international police cooperation, stronger security, teaching people to recognise scams

prompt: In many countries, fewer students are choosing to study science subjects at university. What are the reasons for this? How can more young people be encouraged to study science?
ideas: Science is seen as difficult and boring at school
Other careers seem to offer more money or fame
Solutions: practical lessons, scholarships, showing real-world uses of science

prompt: Some people think that the number of tourists visiting popular cities and natural sites should be strictly limited. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
ideas: Too many visitors damage sites and disturb residents
Limits can protect places for future generations
But tourism is important for jobs and income

prompt: Some people believe that talent, for example in music or sport, is something a person is born with. Others think that any skill can be developed through hard work and practice. Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.
ideas: Some people show unusual ability from a very young age
Top performers almost always practise for thousands of hours
Your view: natural ability helps, but practice decides who succeeds

prompt: In some countries, people now pay for almost everything by card or phone, and cash is rarely used. Do the advantages of a cashless society outweigh the disadvantages?
ideas: Payments are fast, convenient and easy to track
Harder for criminals to steal or hide money
Older and poorer people may be excluded, and personal privacy is reduced

prompt: Many parts of the world are suffering from a shortage of clean water. What are the main causes of this problem, and what measures could be taken to solve it?
ideas: Causes: population growth, climate change and wasteful farming
Pollution from factories makes water unsafe
Solutions: repair old pipes, recycle water, use efficient irrigation

prompt: In many countries, people are working longer hours and have less free time than before. Why is this happening? What effects does it have on individuals and families?
ideas: High living costs and competition for jobs
Phones and email mean work never really stops
Effects: stress, health problems and less time with children

prompt: Some people believe that wealthy nations have a responsibility to give financial help to poorer countries. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
ideas: Rich countries have more resources and global problems affect everyone
Aid can save lives in emergencies
Help like education and trade may work better than money alone

prompt: Some people think that teenagers who commit serious crimes should be punished in the same way as adults. Others believe they should be treated differently because of their age. Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.
ideas: Serious crimes harm victims regardless of the criminal's age
Teenagers are still developing and can change
Prison may make young people more likely to commit crimes again

prompt: Air travel has become much cheaper in recent decades, and many more people now fly regularly. Do the advantages of this outweigh the disadvantages?
ideas: More people can visit family, travel and experience new cultures
Business and tourism benefit
Flights produce a lot of pollution and contribute to climate change

prompt: False information spreads quickly on the internet and can influence people's opinions and decisions. What problems does this cause, and what can be done to solve them?
ideas: Problems: people lose trust in experts and make poor health choices
It can divide society and affect elections
Solutions: fact-checking, platform responsibility, teaching critical thinking in schools

prompt: Many traditional jobs are disappearing because machines and computer programs can now do the work. Why is this happening? Is this a positive or negative development for society?
ideas: Machines are cheaper, faster and do not need breaks
Positive: dangerous and boring work is done by machines
Negative: many workers lose jobs and need retraining
